Under the cue, civilian casualties are primary for 12 models and success for 8; nine models switch from success to civilian casualties, and none switch in the opposite direction.49:T629,The paper proposes a framework, not a new metric. It starts by defining a taxonomy of behavioral correctness assumptions, then operationalizes each assumption through controlled response transformations. The assumptions are split into two groups.

1. Correctness-preserving assumptions: transformations that should not change correctness with respect to the reference, such as paraphrasing, stylistic variation, or equivalent reformulation. A reliable evaluator should assign similar scores before and after the transformation.
2. Correctness-altering assumptions: transformations that should reduce response quality, such as removing relevant information, adding factual errors, introducing logical inconsistency, or injecting irrelevant content. A reliable evaluator should lower the score accordingly.

Two design choices matter. First, the transformations are intended to isolate one property at a time, so score changes are attributable rather than confounded. Second, the framework is evaluator-agnostic: it can probe lexical, character-level, semantic, LLM-based, and hybrid evaluators under the same behavioral test suite. In that sense, the work is closer to a stress-testing methodology than to a leaderboard.

The paper also studies repeat-run variability, evaluator configuration sensitivity, and test-suite reproducibility. These are especially important for LLM judges, whose outputs can vary with prompts, decoding settings, or model versions. An evaluator that looks good on aggregate but is unstable across runs or configurations is risky as a training signal.4a:T445,The empirical study covers a broad range of reference-based evaluators, including lexical overlap methods, character-level methods, semantic similarity methods, LLM-based evaluators, and hybrid systems. The main result is not that one family dominates everywhere, but that assumption-level analysis reveals distinct behavioral profiles that aggregate benchmark scores often hide. Lexical methods tend to be brittle under surface-form changes and therefore violate some correctness-preserving assumptions. Semantic and LLM-based methods are usually more robust to paraphrase, but may be less sensitive to certain correctness-altering transformations or more variable under configuration changes.

The paper also reports stability analyses across repeated runs, evaluator settings, and independently generated test suites. The key takeaway is that the proposed diagnostic framework itself appears reproducible enough to support meaningful evaluator characterization. For practical use, the most informative results are likely the per-assumption breakdowns rather than any averaged summary score.4b:T636,The method has two stages. Stage one builds structured compositional supervision. Instead of crude object swapping, the pipeline starts from real images sampled from LAION-400M. Qwen3-VL-32B extracts a structured scene graph-like description with objects, attributes, and relations. A sampled schema decides how many objects and attributes to keep. Conditioned on this schema and a five-level matching taxonomy, the MLLM generates one retrieval query and five captions. The five levels are: full match, partial presence, attribute error, object error, and full mismatch. Z-Image-Turbo then synthesizes one candidate image per caption, yielding a graded candidate list rather than a flat positive/negative set.

Stage two performs distillation. The synthesized data first fine-tunes a reranker, producing Core-Reranker. Then the reranker’s listwise compositional preferences are distilled into the embedding model, producing Core-Embed. The paper compares standard contrastive learning, pairwise CoSENT, and listwise Rank-KL. The main conclusion is that listwise supervision is the right fit for this setting because the target is not just “correct vs incorrect” but an ordered similarity spectrum. Rank-KL works by matching the embedding-induced ranking distribution to the teacher reranker’s distribution over the whole candidate list. Another useful detail is the diagnostic on Matryoshka dimensions: increasing representation dimension helps binding-sensitive subsets much more than simple lexical substitutions, which motivates distillation beyond merely widening the embedding.4c:T59f,There are three main experimental messages. First, the paper validates the capability gap between reranking and embedding. A representative example shows that both the backbone and the reranker rank fine-grained compositional candidates correctly, while embedding similarity fails. The Matryoshka sweep supports the same story: on two SugarCrepe++ subsets, increasing the representation dimension from 512 to 1536 barely changes Replace Attribute, from 0.773 to 0.777, but improves the more binding-sensitive Swap Attribute from 0.589 to 0.623.

Second, the objective comparison is important. CoSENT and Rank-KL both outperform standard contrastive learning under the five-level supervision, and Rank-KL is the strongest overall. This suggests the gain is not only from better hard negatives, but also from using an objective aligned with ordered supervision.

Third, the end results are solid. Core-Reranker-8B reaches 82.7% total average on compositional reasoning benchmarks, surpassing the previous best reranker. Core-Embed-8B achieves the best total average among evaluated embedding models. On MCMR, Core-Embed-8B improves R@1 from 0.375 to 0.412 over its backbone, while preserving performance on standard retrieval sets such as COCO and Flickr30K. The graded held-out evaluation protocol is also a meaningful contribution because it measures whether the model learns relative compositional similarity, not just binary correctness.4d:T6b4,The method, FactoSR, follows a two-stage recipe: supervised spatial fine-tuning first, then factorized reinforcement learning. In the SFT stage, the model is taught to produce structured outputs that separate observation, localization, reasoning, and final answer. In the RL stage, the authors build on RLVR with GRPO-style optimization, but replace the usual single correctness reward with a multi-objective reward design.

There are five reward components. A format reward keeps outputs structurally valid during RL. An accuracy reward preserves standard final-answer supervision. The key novelty lies in three geometry-aware rewards. The XY reward enforces cross-view planar consistency and correspondence, encouraging the model to identify the correct region before answering. The Z reward targets 3D localization and relative depth ordering, which is critical for front/back, near/far, and occlusion reasoning. The T reward enforces temporal cycle consistency and reversible camera-motion reasoning, pushing the model to remain coherent over sequences rather than treating frames independently.

This is not an architectural change to the backbone. It is a change in task decomposition and training signal design. Relative to prior spatial RLVR work, the differences are clear: it moves from final-answer-only rewards to factorized rewards, from mostly single-view reasoning to multi-view and temporal settings, and from implicit language-space reasoning to explicitly geometry-constrained optimization. The trade-off is also clear: the approach depends on datasets and annotations that support verifiable XY/Z/T rewards, so scalability and transfer will depend on how broadly those rewards can be instantiated.4e:T59b,The headline results reported in the paper are gains of 5.9% on VSI-Bench and 4.5% on All-Angles-Bench, while maintaining decent general multimodal capability. The experimental story is less about one benchmark and more about whether the factorized rewards produce separable gains on separable spatial skills.

The key ablations compare SFT only, SFT plus standard RLVR, and SFT plus FactoSR-RL. The paper’s main claim is that answer-only RL helps somewhat, but remains unstable on depth, cross-view correspondence, and temporal consistency. Adding XY/Z/T rewards yields larger improvements on tasks that require explicit geometric reasoning chains. Reward ablations further support the decomposition: removing XY hurts cross-view localization and correspondence; removing Z weakens relative depth and occlusion judgments; removing T degrades camera-motion and temporal reverse-reasoning tasks. The authors also emphasize stronger generalization than pure SFT, arguing that RL encourages strategy learning rather than memorization of static patterns.

From the provided full-text excerpt, there is no reliable complete table of model size, training steps, or dataset scale, so those details should not be overstated. What is clear is that this is an SFT-plus-RL enhancement on top of an existing VLM, with the main contribution in reward design and spatial-temporal data construction rather than large-scale pretraining from scratch.4f:T652,DART stands for Depth-as-Target. The central design is to augment DINOv2 with a pixel-space depth reconstruction head, so the model keeps DINOv2’s self-distillation-based representation learning while also predicting pseudo depth maps. The key choice is what the paper does not do: it does not build an RGB-D encoder that requires depth at inference, and it does not follow the standard MAE-style route of feeding depth as an input modality. Instead, depth is used as auxiliary supervision during pretraining only. This matches the deployment constraint in surgery, where reliable depth input is often unavailable.

The motivation in the paper is comparative. Off-the-shelf DINOv2 and DINOv3 pretrained on natural images do not transfer well enough to surgical imagery. MAE-family methods, including RGB-D variants such as MultiMAE, also fail to close the gap in the authors’ setting; the paper explicitly notes that MultiMAE underperforms a single-modality MAE baseline in their surgical pretraining setup. That negative result is important because it justifies moving depth supervision into a DINOv2-style framework rather than continuing along the MAE path.

Technically, the training objective is a combination of the original DINOv2 objective and a depth reconstruction loss. The depth supervision comes from off-the-shelf pseudo-labeled dense depth rather than real depth sensors, which lowers the data barrier and makes the recipe scalable. The contribution is therefore not a new architecture but a domain-aware pretraining recipe that injects geometric supervision without changing inference requirements.50:T47e,From the provided full-content excerpt, several experimental comparisons are clear. First, the paper compares off-the-shelf DINOv2/DINOv3, surgically adapted DINOv2, MAE, and RGB-D MAE variants, and concludes that natural-image VFMs transfer poorly while the DINOv2 route is the better starting point in this domain. Second, the paper explicitly reports a negative result: MultiMAE underperforms a single-modality MAE baseline in their surgical setting, which supports the decision not to use depth as an encoder input. Third, DART is intended to improve both dense pixel-level tasks and image-level tasks, so the evaluation is framed as multi-task transfer rather than a single downstream benchmark.

However, the excerpt provided here does not include the full result tables, exact dataset sizes, backbone scales, training budgets, or precise gains. Without those sections, it would be unsafe to invent numbers. What can be stated confidently is that the experimental argument is built around recipe comparison and transfer breadth, with DART positioned as a better surgical pretraining recipe than RGB-only DINOv2 and MAE-style RGB-D alternatives.51:Te4a,整体架构由三部分组成：一个基于 LLaDA 2.0 的冻结 dLLM-VLM 负责多模态理解，一个 connector 把理解侧 hidden states 投到生成条件空间，一个 6B 单流 Diffusion Transformer 负责图像合成。关键点不在“模块很多”，而在职责边界划得很清楚。

1. 先学视觉先验，再学语言对齐
作者反对从训练一开始就重度依赖图文对。原因有两个：一是 caption 贵且噪声大；二是在低分辨率训练阶段，caption 中描述的细节常因下采样而不可见，导致条件和目标不匹配。为此，他们先做 image-only pre-training 和 mid-training，让 DiT 先把自然图像分布学扎实。这里不是无条件生成，而是借助冻结 VLM 从“同一图像区域”提取条件表示，让条件和生成目标天然对齐，避免外部 caption 带来的语义漂移。这个设计很像在做一种自蒸馏式的视觉条件建模：监督信号主要来自真实图像本身，语言只在后期逐步接入。

2. 统一理解、生成、编辑，但不强行共用所有路径
文本生成和编辑共用同一条语义条件路径：文本、视觉上下文和结构化 reasoning trace 先进入 dLLM-VLM，再经 Residual Query Adapter 和轻量 Transformer connector 送入 DiT。编辑任务则额外引入 reference-image pathway，而且这个路径直接进 DiT，绕过 VLM。作者这样做的原因很实际：编辑时既需要高层语义指令，也需要像素级或局部外观证据；如果全部压进 VLM hidden states，参考图像细节容易损失。因此他们同时使用 SigLIP-VQ 特征和 clean VAE latent，分别提供语义级和像素级参考信号。这个设计说明作者没有把“统一”理解成单一路径，而是按信息类型分层接入。

3. progressive training pipeline
训练分阶段推进：先在 256 分辨率做 image-only pre-training；再做 aspect-ratio-bucketed mid-training，继续扩展视觉先验；之后在 512 和 1024 分辨率引入 paired language alignment；再对 text-rich 和 portrait 数据做 targeted refinement；最后做 generation-editing joint training。这里有两个关键取舍。其一，数据配比上始终保持 real-data-dominant，整条生成训练链约 2.2 亿样本，其中 98% 是真实图像，SFT 阶段真实图像占比也保持在 70% 以上。作者承认这种路线在早期 benchmark 收敛可能慢于 synthetic-heavy 配方，但长期 realism ceiling 更高。其二，训练目标不是一次性混训所有能力，而是按“先分布、后条件、再任务整合”的顺序推进，这和大模型训练里常见的 annealing / curriculum 思路一致。

4. 稳定性与优化
DiT 全面使用 parameter-free RMSNorm，而不是带可学习缩放参数的归一化。作者的意图是减少大模型 diffusion 训练中的尺度漂移和额外不稳定因素。优化器选 Muon，也是在强调大规模从头训练的稳定与效率。虽然从给出的片段里看不到完整优化细节和对比表，但论文把这两点列为 recipe 的核心组成，说明它们不是边角工程，而是支撑 6B DiT 训练成功的重要条件。

5. TwinFlow 蒸馏到 Turbo
部署侧使用 TwinFlow，把原始多步 diffusion 模型蒸馏成 2–4 步的 LLaDA-Image Turbo。方法上结合了 distribution-matching distillation 和 self-adversarial flow training。值得注意的是，作者把 Turbo 视为同一家族的部署变体，而不是另起一个轻量模型。这意味着训练时就考虑了 teacher 分布是否适合后续 few-step student 拟合，属于“为蒸馏而设计主模型”的思路。52:T65f,This is highly relevant to foundation-model pretraining. Its significance is not just that it trains a 6B DiT, but that it makes several training decisions explicit and backs them with a full recipe. Four contributions stand out.

First, it argues clearly for decoupling visual-prior learning from language alignment. The generator is trained to model image distribution first, and paired supervision is introduced later. That is closely analogous to the separation between broad pretraining and later alignment in LLMs, and it is a useful design pattern for multimodal foundation training.

Second, it shows a concrete role for a diffusion language model beyond understanding alone. The frozen LLaDA2.0-Mini-based VLM acts as a semantic conditioning hub that unifies text, visual context, and reasoning traces. This gives a practical answer to how an understanding model and a generation model can be separated without becoming disconnected.

Third, the paper contributes a serious large-scale training recipe: parameter-free RMSNorm throughout the DiT, the Muon optimizer, and a progressive curriculum over data type and resolution. For training large DiTs from scratch, these choices matter more than many cosmetic architectural tweaks.

Fourth, few-step distillation is treated as part of the main model family rather than an afterthought. In that sense, LLaDA-Image is not just a model but a full pipeline from prior learning to alignment, editing, and deployment. This should matter for open image-generation pretraining, and it also has direct relevance to unified multimodal pretraining and AR-plus-diffusion style systems.53:T1037,The system has three main components: a frozen dLLM-based VLM built on LLaDA 2.0 for multimodal understanding, a connector that projects understanding-side hidden states into the generator conditioning space, and a 6B single-stream Diffusion Transformer for image synthesis. The key is not the number of modules, but the clarity of their roles.

1. Learn the visual prior first, then align to language.
The authors explicitly avoid heavy dependence on paired image-text data at the beginning of training. Their argument is practical: captions are expensive and noisy, and at low training resolutions many captioned details are no longer visible after downsampling, which creates condition-target mismatch. Instead, they begin with image-only pretraining and mid-training so that the DiT first learns the natural image distribution well. This is not purely unconditional generation. A frozen VLM extracts conditioning signals from the same image region that the DiT is asked to generate, which keeps condition and target tightly matched without relying on external captions. Conceptually, this resembles a form of self-distilled visual conditioning: the image itself provides most of the supervision signal, while language is introduced later.

2. Unify understanding, generation, and editing without forcing a single pathway for everything.
Text-to-image generation and editing share the same semantic conditioning route: text, visual context, and structured reasoning traces are encoded by the dLLM-VLM, then passed through a Residual Query Adapter and a lightweight Transformer connector into the DiT. Editing adds a separate reference-image pathway that goes directly into the DiT and bypasses the VLM. This is an important design choice. Editing needs both high-level semantic instructions and low-level appearance evidence; if everything is compressed into VLM hidden states, reference fidelity can be lost. To address this, the model uses both SigLIP-VQ features and clean VAE latents, providing semantic-level and pixel-level reference signals respectively. The paper’s notion of unification is therefore layered rather than monolithic.

3. Progressive training pipeline.
Training proceeds in stages: image-only pretraining at 256 resolution, aspect-ratio-bucketed mid-training to strengthen the visual prior, paired language alignment at 512 and 1024 resolution, targeted refinement on text-rich and portrait data, and finally joint generation-editing training. Two design choices matter here. First, the data mixture remains real-data-dominant throughout. The full generation pipeline processes about 220M samples, 98% of them real images, and the real-image share stays above 70% even during supervised fine-tuning. The authors explicitly acknowledge that this may converge more slowly on early benchmarks than synthetic-heavy mixtures, but they argue that it yields stronger realism at convergence. Second, capabilities are not mixed all at once. The curriculum follows a distribution-first, conditioning-next, task-integration-later order, which is very much in line with annealing and curriculum ideas in large-model training.

4. Stability and optimization.
The DiT uses parameter-free RMSNorm throughout rather than a learnable affine normalization. The motivation is to reduce scale drift and unnecessary instability in large-scale diffusion training. The optimizer is Muon, again chosen with training stability and scalability in mind. The provided excerpt does not include the full optimization ablations, but the paper presents these choices as central parts of the recipe rather than minor implementation details.

5. TwinFlow distillation to Turbo.
For deployment, the original multi-step model is distilled into 2–4-step LLaDA-Image Turbo variants using TwinFlow, which combines distribution-matching distillation with self-adversarial flow training. An important point is that Turbo is treated as a deployment variant within the same family, not as a separate lightweight model. This suggests that the teacher is trained with downstream few-step distillation in mind, which is a more integrated view of training and serving.54:T8fd,The experimental results support several distinct claims.

First, on overall capability, LLaDA-Image performs strongly on Qwen-Image-Bench, LongText-Bench, CVTG-2K, and GEdit-Bench, covering photorealism, prompt alignment, bilingual Chinese-English text rendering, and instruction-guided editing. The emphasis is on balanced capability rather than optimizing a single aesthetic metric. That matters because many open models still lag badly on text rendering or reference-preserving editing.

Second, the data strategy is a central empirical result. The paper argues that image-only pretraining followed by progressive language alignment is not only viable, but preferable in the long run to synthetic-heavy paired training from the start. Synthetic mixtures may improve early benchmark numbers faster, but they also inject artifacts and caption bias that hurt realism later. The full generation pipeline uses about 220M samples, with more than 90% of training in image-only stages and 98% of samples coming from real images. Those numbers make the intended shift in supervision very concrete.

Third, the system scale and deployment profile are explicit. The main generator is a 6B DiT trained from scratch, while the understanding module is built on a frozen LLaDA2.0-Mini backbone. The release includes four checkpoints: Base and Turbo, plus FP8 variants of each. The Turbo models run with only 2–4 sampling steps, which substantially lowers inference cost.

Fourth, editing performance comes from the unified architecture rather than a separate editing backbone. Text-to-image and editing share the semantic path, while reference images are injected through an additional DiT-side pathway. This allows the model to balance instruction following and reference preservation on editing benchmarks such as GEdit-Bench. That is an important result for unified multimodal generation systems, where many models still trade off editability against fidelity.

The provided excerpt does not include full score tables, FID values, or detailed human-evaluation numbers, so those should not be fabricated. The reliable hard facts are: a 6B DiT, roughly 220M training samples, 98% real images, more than 90% image-only training stages, more than 70% real-image share during SFT, and 2–4-step Turbo inference.55:T74e,This one deserves a careful read. Do not start from the benchmark tables. Start with the introduction and model design, because the paper is really about training philosophy and system decomposition. The three questions to keep in mind are: why learn the visual prior before language alignment, why route editing through an extra reference path instead of only through the VLM, and why insist on a real-data-dominant recipe.

A good reading order is:
1. Introduction: identify the three main threads—data decoupling, unified architecture, and few-step deployment.
2. Model Design: focus on the interfaces among the frozen dLLM-VLM, the Residual Query Adapter, the connector, and the single-stream DiT. This is where the division of labor between understanding and generation becomes clear.
3. Training pipeline: this is the most valuable section for pretraining researchers. Pay close attention to stage boundaries, data composition, resolution transitions, when paired data is introduced, and how refinement data is selected.
4. Stability and optimization details: look for the rationale and any ablations behind parameter-free RMSNorm and Muon, especially whether they matter more at larger batch sizes, higher resolutions, or longer training runs.
5. Editing and Turbo distillation: if you care about unified multimodal generation or deployment, read these sections closely, especially the reference pathway and the TwinFlow objective.
6. Experiments: prioritize ablations on data mixture, the necessity of the image-only stages, the effect of real-data ratio on realism and alignment, and the quality-speed trade-off between the original model and Turbo.

If time is limited, spend at least 60–90 minutes on the method and training recipe. If you work on diffusion LMs, unified multimodal pretraining, or AR-plus-diffusion systems, this is worth taking notes on.56:T452,The authors formulate OPD as training on on-policy autoregressive states s=(x, y_<i). The student samples rollouts under its current policy, and the teacher supplies a next-token distribution at each visited prefix. The student is then updated toward the teacher on those visited states, typically through a token-level KL or cross-entropy loss. The key move is to treat a query as a generator of states, not as a single training item. To quantify this, the paper defines state coverage: states visited by full-data OPD are grouped into semantic clusters, and a query set is scored by the fraction of those clusters reached by its rollouts. This avoids exact-prefix matching, which would be too sparse, and gives a better proxy for the supervision OPD actually sees. The second diagnostic is absorption rate, the fraction of the remaining teacher-student gap closed by one update. This separates insufficient data coverage from slow algorithmic uptake. The paper then tests the same account in multi-teacher OPD, off-domain prompting, content-free prompting, and a controlled comparison with one-shot RLVR.57:T4ad,The phenomenon is tested across four task domains and three model families. One-shot OPD continues to improve for hundreds of optimization steps and recovers most of the full-data OPD gain, even in cases where the student never solves the training query. The full-data reference contains about 17k queries. The most important measurement is state coverage: one query already reaches 71.5% of the states visited by full-data OPD, with most of that coverage appearing within the first 100 steps. Sixteen semantically diverse queries reach 98.9% coverage and match full-data training. The absorption-rate analysis shows similar decay patterns for one-shot and full-data OPD, indicating that the run length is governed more by how slowly OPD absorbs dense teacher supervision than by a lack of new prompts. In multi-teacher OPD, 16 diverse queries per domain are enough to match full-data training. Off-domain WildChat prompts and content-free templates remain nearly as effective as the full training set. In a controlled one-shot comparison, OPD achieves more than twice the validation gain of RLVR over 1000 steps because its token-level signal persists after the outcome reward has been exhausted.58:T46f,Read it closely. Start with the Introduction for the paper’s decomposition into state supply and absorption rate. Then inspect the OPD objective and the definition of state, since the paper’s state is an autoregressive prefix rather than a high-level environment state. The main empirical phenomenon is in Section 3; focus on whether the one-shot gain could be explained by memorization, solved trajectories, or model-family artifacts. Section 4 is the core section: read the state-coverage construction, the semantic clustering procedure, the 71.5% single-query result, the 98.9% sixteen-query result, and the diverse-query selection ablations. Section 5 is the second key section because absorption rate is what supports the claim that OPD is limited by uptake speed. Sections 6 and 7 are useful for generalization: multi-teacher routing, content-free prompts, off-domain prompts, and the RLVR comparison all test whether the state-level explanation survives outside the one-shot setup. If available, the appendix details on clustering, rollout sampling, teacher-logit access, temperature, and query selection are worth checking.59:T543,LeanGRPO removes update-stage recomputation through a systems redesign with two pieces. First, it changes the data-parallel layout. Instead of assigning different prompts to different GPUs and generating multiple local samples per prompt, all GPUs process the same prompt while each rank generates a different sample. This reduces the need for each rank to retain multiple computation graphs for the same prompt group.

Second, it introduces two recompute-free schedules. LeanGRPO-Retain simply enables gradient tracking during rollout and keeps the selected-timestep graphs alive until terminal rewards and group advantages are available, then reuses those graphs for backpropagation. It is simple but activation memory grows with the number of selected timesteps.

LeanGRPO-Reweight is more subtle. During rollout, each selected-timestep graph is immediately consumed through a provisional backward pass, producing a provisional gradient and allowing saved activations to be released right away. Once the terminal reward and advantage are known, the provisional gradient is corrected using that advantage, recovering the same policy gradient in exact arithmetic. This shifts the memory burden from retained activations to stored provisional gradients. The paper positions both schedules as objective-preserving rather than approximate shortcuts.5a:T8bb,文章的核心设计是把 supervision 当成“随训练演化的状态”，而不是固定标签。围绕这个抽象，框架分成三个模块，但作者强调它们是互补的 intervention points，不是必须串行执行的流水线。

第一块是 Active Data Selection。目标是在训练预算和标注预算有限时，决定哪些样本进入训练、哪些样本需要外部标注、哪些样本转入弱监督路径。实现上覆盖 verified difficulty filtering、基于模型不确定性的选择、以及 probe-calibrated selection 等。这里的关键不是某一种打分器，而是把“是否值得花 rollout/annotation 成本”前置成显式决策。

第二块是 Weak Supervision Construction。它让无标注样本也能参与 RLVR，包括伪目标构造、cross-view agreement、以及 target-free reward 等机制。文中把 TTRL、Co-Rewarding、EMRL、Intuitor 这类方法都纳入同一接口。这样做的意义在于，弱监督不再需要重写整套 rollout-optimization loop，而是作为 supervision semantics 的一种实现被注入。

第三块是 Training-Time Supervision Refinement。训练过程中，已有监督或构造监督可能因为噪声、策略漂移、奖励黑客等问题变得不可靠，因此框架支持基于 reward dynamics、表示几何、rollout evidence 的在线重估和修正，对应 TraPO、GeoMin、online label refinement 等方法。这里最重要的思想是：监督质量不是离线一次性决定的，而应在 policy 改变后被重新审视。

工程上，DE-Venus 采用“minimal-invasion”设计，保留 verl 作为 rollout、优化、验证、checkpoint 的执行底座，只在 supervision 语义发生变化的边界处插入模块。数据层用统一的 Parquet 约定记录样本身份和监督状态；训练批次则以 verl 兼容格式携带 targets、rewards、selection、advantages 等字段。再配合 voting、verification、uncertainty estimation、reward construction、evidence analysis、validation logging 等可复用服务，达到方法解耦和后端复用。这个设计选择比单个算法细节更重要，因为它决定了不同 RLVR 方法能否在同一系统里做 apples-to-apples 比较。5b:T94b,The central idea is to model supervision as evolving state rather than fixed labels. On top of that abstraction, the framework organizes the lifecycle into three modules, which are presented as complementary intervention points rather than a mandatory sequential pipeline.

The first module is Active Data Selection. It decides which examples should be retained for training, which should receive external labels, and which should be routed to weak supervision. Implementations include verified-difficulty filtering, model-based uncertainty selection, and probe-calibrated selection. The important design choice is that budget allocation is made explicit before expensive rollout and annotation are spent.

The second module is Weak Supervision Construction. It allows unlabeled examples to participate in RLVR by constructing pseudo-targets, enforcing agreement across views, or assigning target-free rewards. The framework covers methods such as TTRL, Co-Rewarding, EMRL, and Intuitor under a shared interface. This matters because weak supervision no longer requires rewriting the rollout-to-update loop; it becomes a localized change in supervision semantics.

The third module is Training-Time Supervision Refinement. Since supervision can become unreliable due to noise, policy drift, or reward hacking, the framework supports online reassessment and revision using reward dynamics, representation geometry, and rollout evidence. This includes methods such as TraPO, GeoMin, and online label refinement. The deeper point is that supervision quality should be revisited as the policy changes, not fixed once offline.

At the systems level, DE-Venus follows a minimal-invasion design. It keeps verl as the execution substrate for rollout generation, optimization, validation, and checkpointing, and inserts method-specific logic only at the boundaries where supervision semantics change. Persistent sample identity and supervision state are stored through a shared Parquet convention, while verl-compatible batches carry targets, rewards, selections, and advantages during online optimization. Reusable services handle voting, verification, uncertainty estimation, reward construction, evidence analysis, and validation logging. This architecture is arguably the main contribution because it enables apples-to-apples comparisons across heterogeneous RLVR supervision methods.5c:T535,From the provided full-text excerpt, the framework includes reproducible implementations for seven representative methods plus an active data-selection pipeline, and it is evaluated on public reasoning benchmarks as well as three business scenarios. The experimental goal is not to claim that one new algorithm dominates all others. Instead, it is to show that a unified framework can host multiple supervision regimes, reproduce them on a common backend, and improve data efficiency under realistic RLVR constraints.

The abstract indicates that on standard math and general reasoning benchmarks, DE-Venus can preserve or improve RLVR effectiveness while reducing annotation or rollout cost. It also claims practical benefits from decoupling supervision logic from distributed execution, making method switching and controlled comparison easier. The excerpt does not include the full numeric tables, so exact gains, budget reductions, or benchmark scores should not be fabricated here.

Additional experiments on coding reasoning, Llama models, and other algorithmic settings are used to check that the phenomenon is not limited to Qwen3 math training.5f:T5d4,RISE constructs a synthetic teacher by extrapolating the displacement between a current RLVR-updated checkpoint and a trailing anchor checkpoint. Let π_{θ_n} be the policy at iteration n, updated by RLVR to π_{θ'_{n+1}}. Choose a representation map φ that embeds a policy into a vector space where linear operations are meaningful (parameters or logits/distributions). Define the recent improvement direction as Δ = φ(π_{θ'_{n+1}}) − φ(π_{θ_n}). The self-extrapolated teacher is obtained by projecting further along this direction with scale β:

φ(teacher) = φ(π_{θ'_{n+1}}) + (β−1)·Δ, with β>1.

Two instantiations are emphasized:
- Weight-space extrapolation (φ=θ): θ_future = θ'_{n+1} + (β−1)(θ'_{n+1}−θ_n), essentially task arithmetic with an extrapolation coefficient; the teacher is an explicit model.
- Logit-space extrapolation (φ=logits / next-token distributions): extrapolate at the output distribution level (implemented via a geometric mixture / distributional extrapolation), producing token-level targets without necessarily materializing a full parameter-space teacher.

Training alternates RLVR and OPD in a recursive loop: RLVR grounds the direction (so extrapolation is not amplifying arbitrary drift), and OPD distills the extrapolated teacher into the student via token-level KL/CE. Key design knobs are β, anchor lag, and the choice of φ, each trading off compute, stability, and how “local” the teacher remains to the student.60:T526,An end-to-end pipeline:
- Web-graph construction: represent a web corpus as a directed hyperlink graph; improve out-link recall by merging a semantic mirror (RDF triples) with rendered markup.
- Task synthesis: sample an answer-anchored seed page, expand to a local subgraph, distill noisy pages into a connected entity graph, then generate a multi-hop question over that graph.
- Anchor removal / entity rewriting: abstract away directly searchable anchors so the task requires evidence composition across hops rather than single-query lookup.
- Dual-criteria verification: keep only tasks that are both sufficiently difficult and objectively checkable.
- Trajectory collection + filtering: roll out a strong teacher, then apply multi-stage filtering at both trajectory and turn levels to remove low-signal steps (irrelevant browsing, broken evidence chains, hallucinated citations).
- Training: start with filtered SFT; then do RL against live web search with an in-cluster judge and an observation summarizer; use iterative “SFT–RL climbing” where successful RL rollouts are fed back into the next SFT round to stabilize learning and improve sample efficiency.

OPD supervises the student on trajectories sampled from the current student policy, matching the student distribution to the teacher distribution along student-generated prefixes. The paper starts from the sequence-level reverse KL and uses its exact token-level decomposition. In practice, the main implementation is student top-k OPD: at each step, compute the KL only over the k tokens with highest student probability, after renormalizing both student and teacher on that subset. This choice is practical: much cheaper than full-vocabulary KL, but denser than sampled-token supervision.

On top of this setup, the paper runs three layers of analysis. First is 1-shot OPD: sample a single training example and ask whether training on only that example can still improve the student, and whether it overfits. Second is difficulty analysis: bucket examples by difficulty and compare the downstream gains from easy, medium, and hard subsets, including examples beyond the capability frontier of both teacher and student. Third is mechanism analysis: test whether the gains are explained by high token entropy or by long CoT trajectories. The evidence supports the latter. The pipeline has only two stages. The executor produces an initial answer A0. The reviewer sees the problem and A0, then emits accept/reject plus a written critique. If rejected, the executor revises once to produce A1. There is no planner stage, specifically to avoid extra confounds.

The key methodological choice is a paired design. The executor solves each problem once, and the exact same A0 is reviewed under every reviewer condition. This removes executor sampling variance from condition-to-condition comparisons. The four conditions are: no review, self-review, a cross-family mid-tier reviewer, and a weak reviewer. The executor is Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite with 52% standalone accuracy on the task set. The mid-tier reviewer is gpt-oss-20b. The main contribution is not a new pipeline architecture but the rejection-outcome decomposition. Instead of counting rejections or final accuracy alone, the paper tracks what each rejection actually did: fix a wrong answer, damage a correct one, fail because the executor ignored the critique, or induce a wrong correction. This decomposition exposes two common evaluation mistakes. High rejection rate does not imply useful review, and low observed damage does not imply reviewer quality if the executor simply refuses to follow bad critiques. In other words, reviewer quality and critique uptake are separate variables and must be analyzed separately.65:T69e,The headline result is straightforward. The fixed executor solves 52 out of 100 Olympiad math problems correctly. Replacing no-review with a cross-family mid-tier reviewer raises final accuracy to 64%, a gain of 12 percentage points with p=0.0005, and with zero damaged correct answers. This shows that a reviewer does not need full task-solving ability to create net value if it can reject the right cases.

Self-review is the more revealing condition. It achieves the highest detection rate, yet yields no significant accuracy gain. The paper reports that self-review rejects about 2.1 times as often as the effective mid-tier reviewer, but repairs only about one-third as many answers. It also falsely rejects 35% of the executor’s correct answers. The crucial detail is what happens after those false rejections: whenever the executor actually follows the critique, the revised answer becomes wrong. Cases that appear harmless are harmless only because the executor ignored the critique. This is the empirical basis for the paper’s claim that apparent self-review safety is often revision inertia in disguise.

At the low end, the weak reviewer is effectively inert. It changes none of the 100 final answers while roughly doubling token cost. That gives a practical capability floor: below some threshold, review neither repairs errors nor triggers useful revisions, and only adds overhead.

There is also an implementation detail worth noting. An initial run revealed truncation in the mid-tier reviewer’s outputs, so token limits were adjusted and documented. First, the authors recover the prior direction. Given the unembedding matrix W and an empirical unigram distribution p_unigram, they solve a linear least-squares problem over the frequent-token subset to find a vector d_prior such that softmax(W d_prior) reconstructs the unigram distribution as closely as possible. This requires only the output weights and token counts from a corpus, with no model forward passes. They argue that the recovered direction is unique under the fitting procedure and show that it is absent at random initialization but emerges through training. Second, they derive a tempered Bayesian interpretation. For any final prediction state y_pred, they decompose it into λ d_prior plus an orthogonal component. Plugging this into the softmax yields a factorization of the predictive distribution into a unigram prior raised to the power λ times a context-dependent likelihood term. This gives λ a clean probabilistic meaning: λ=0 removes the prior, 0<λ<1 tempers it, λ>1 sharpens it, and λ<0 inverts it. Third, they validate the mechanism dynamically and causally. They vary contextual informativeness through coherent context, shuffled tokens, short contexts, and ambiguous prompts, and track λ. They also intervene directly on the prediction state along d_prior and compare against norm-matched random-direction perturbations to test whether this axis is functionally special.68:T59b,The experiments cover Llama, Qwen, Gemma, and Pythia, from 0.4B to 405B parameters. Four results matter most. First, existence and universality: a single direction reconstructs the unigram prior with low KL error across all tested families, suggesting this is not an artifact of one architecture or recipe. The paper also shows that the direction is not present at initialization and appears only after training. Second, context dynamics: λ decreases as coherent information accumulates, but not merely when token count grows. Shuffled or semantically weak contexts do not reduce λ in the same way, which supports the claim that λ tracks information rather than length or position. Third, causal intervention: increasing the projection along d_prior pushes predictions toward the unigram prior, while decreasing it makes predictions rely more on contextual evidence. Random directions with matched magnitude do not produce the same effect, so d_prior is not just a post hoc statistical fit. The technical contribution has two main parts.

First, it separates the static and dynamic descriptions. In the high-dimensional limit d→∞, the population loss is shown to depend on only finitely many trace-type order parameters, even though the original parameter space is Θ(d^2). So the loss landscape admits a finite-dimensional macroscopic description. However, online SGD is richer: for both tied and untied factorizations, the updates generate an infinite hierarchy of joint matrix moments, and no fixed finite set closes the dynamics in general. The authors then prove that the empirical trajectory converges to a deterministic infinite-dimensional ODE, and that finite-order truncations approximate this limiting dynamics with exponentially decaying error. This is the key methodological result.

Second, the paper analyzes parameterization-induced implicit bias by comparing three representations of the same effective attention: direct optimization of S, tied factorization S=WW^T, and untied factorization S=UV^T. Direct optimization suffers from an information-exponent bottleneck: when first-order correlation vanishes, SGD can remain trapped in an uninformative phase on the d^2 log d sample scale. In the tied case, the PSD structure provides an automatic symmetry-breaking mechanism. Under a mild non-degeneracy condition, this enables weak recovery at Θ(d^2 log d) samples. In the untied case, the mechanism is different: there is a fast-slow decomposition. Quantities such as 1/sqrt(d) Tr(UV^T) evolve on a fast timescale and create a boundary layer; the slower matrix-moment dynamics then proceed from the state selected by that fast transient. Weak recovery occurs only if this early shift breaks the relevant symmetry.6c:T5e8,The empirical component is mainly numerical validation of the theory rather than large-scale model benchmarking. The important results are threefold.

First, the paper shows that finite-order truncations of the infinite moment hierarchy provide accurate approximations, with error decreasing rapidly as the truncation order increases. This supports the practical tractability of the otherwise infinite-dimensional ODE description.

Second, it compares the three parameterizations under uninformative initialization. Direct optimization of S remains bottlenecked when first-order correlation is absent. The tied PSD factorization achieves weak recovery on the Θ(d^2 log d) sample scale. The untied factorization can either recover or remain uninformative, depending on which symmetry branch is selected during the fast boundary-layer dynamics. The important takeaway is the difference in phase behavior and sample complexity, not a single benchmark number.

Third, numerical trajectories match the theoretical ODE predictions, indicating that the high-dimensional limit is not merely formal. The paper also highlights a sharp distinction from finite-rank sequence-indexed models, where a finite set of order parameters often closes the dynamics; here it does not.

Each model tokenizes the same text with its own tokenizer, and a window aligner constructs spans whose decoded text matches across models, producing aligned residual-stream activations. Each model’s encoder maps its activation into the common latent dictionary. For latent selection, the method normalizes selection scores across models, sums the normalized votes, and applies a joint TopK to choose one shared index set. The selected magnitudes are not normalized, so each model retains its activation scale information. Each model reconstructs its own activation with its own decoder, and a cross-stream rescaling term makes codes from one model reconstruct other models’ activations, tying the same latent index to similar features across models. During training, vote-source dropout selects the TopK indices from a randomly chosen single model with probability 0.5, which makes solo-model inference in-distribution. 后半部分把这个模板推广到 KL-regularized RL、OPD 和 test-time search。虽然给出的全文片段主要覆盖 Part I，但从摘要与行文结构可以看出，作者采用的是统一的 Gibbs posterior 形式：q*(y|x) ∝ π_ref(y|x) exp(U(x,y)/β)，其中 U 可以是 log-likelihood、reward、advantage 或 search-induced utility。SFT 对应 U=log q_data 或等价的 teacher log-density；KL-regularized RL 对应 reward-weighted posterior；OPD 则是在 student on-policy 轨迹上，用 teacher 分布去近似某个参考后验；search / CoT 则可被看成 test-time 对 latent reasoning path 的 posterior reweighting。这个统一视角的关键区别在于，它不把这些方法按“训练范式”分开，而是按“先验 + 效用 + 近似器”来分解。这样能更清楚地解释：为什么 reverse-KL 风格的 policy matching 往往 mode-seeking，为什么 SFT 的 forward-KL 更像覆盖 teacher 支持集，以及为什么 few-shot demonstrations 有时像给 posterior 提供额外观测，有时却会和 RL 后的 policy 发生冲突。74:T46f,This note is not proposing a new training recipe. It is trying to give a single probabilistic lens for several procedures that are usually discussed separately: few-shot ICL, SFT, KL-regularized RL, on-policy distillation, and test-time search / chain-of-thought. The central claim is that they can all be written in the same two-step pattern: first construct a generalized Bayes or Gibbs posterior from a prior/reference policy plus a utility signal; then fit a parametric model or policy to approximate that posterior or its posterior predictive. The paper focuses on two key identifications. First, under a hierarchical task distribution, few-shot ICL targets the Bayes posterior predictive. Second, SFT is a forward-KL projection onto a teacher conditional distribution, while KL-regularized RL and OPD approximate reward- or advantage-reweighted posteriors under a reference policy. The framework is meant to explain why ICL and SFT can partially substitute for each other, why few-shot prompting can behave oddly on RL-tuned reasoning models, and why OPD, RLHF/RLVR, and search-based inference are less disjoint than they appear.75:T436,Its value for pretraining research is conceptual rather than algorithmic. It gives a cleaner interface between pretraining, post-training, and test-time adaptation by forcing three questions: what is the target distribution, what role does the prior/reference model play, and whether training and inference-time search are approximating the same posterior or optimizing different objects. For pretraining researchers, two points matter. First, ICL is framed not as a prompting trick but as amortized Bayesian inference learned during pretraining; that changes how one thinks about task mixtures, context structure, and data organization. Second, the differences among SFT, OPD, and KL-regularized RL become easier to localize: KL direction, posterior temperature, utility definition, and approximation family. That helps explain why some post-training signals preserve the pretraining distribution while others overwrite it more aggressively. The contribution is moderate in scale and mostly about unification, but it is useful for thinking about the pretrain↔post-train loop.76:T806,The paper is a theory-oriented note. Part I starts from standard SFT and rewrites conditional maximum likelihood as a forward-KL projection onto the true teacher conditional q_true(y|x): minimizing expected negative log-likelihood is equivalent to minimizing E_x[KL(q_true(.|x) || p_theta(.|x))] up to an entropy term independent of the model parameters. This matters because it makes SFT explicitly a problem of approximating a target conditional distribution. The paper then introduces a hierarchical Bayesian task model: sample a task function f, then sample within-task demonstrations D_k and a query. For any in-context predictor M(D_k, x), the Bayes posterior predictive is the unique minimizer of expected log-loss. If a Transformer is pretrained over the same task distribution, then in the infinite-data/infinite-capacity limit its optimal predictor is exactly that posterior predictive. The point is not merely to restate “ICL is Bayes,” but to place ICL and SFT inside the same language of target-distribution approximation.

The later sections extend the same template to KL-regularized RL, OPD, and test-time search. The visible excerpt mainly covers Part I, but the abstract and setup make the intended form clear: q*(y|x) ∝ π_ref(y|x) exp(U(x,y)/β), where U can be log-likelihood, reward, advantage, or a search-induced utility. SFT corresponds to a likelihood-defined target; KL-regularized RL corresponds to a reward-weighted posterior; OPD can be viewed as fitting the student to a teacher-defined posterior on student-generated trajectories; and search / CoT acts like posterior reweighting over latent reasoning paths at inference time. The useful decomposition is not by training stage but by prior, utility, temperature, and approximation family. That decomposition clarifies why reverse-KL style policy matching is often mode-seeking, why forward-KL SFT is more support-covering, and why few-shot demonstrations sometimes behave like extra observations for posterior updating but can also conflict with an RL-shaped policy.77:T6da,The method has two modules. GUT-Q is the uncertainty quantification component. For a given problem, the model is sampled multiple times to produce multiple reasoning chains. The chains are then merged into a directed acyclic graph by identifying semantically equivalent reasoning steps with an NLI model. Nodes represent step-level semantic states; edges represent possible transitions between steps. This is the key move: instead of scoring each sampled chain independently, the method approximates the latent reasoning space induced by token-level stochasticity.

On top of that graph, the paper defines graph complexity as a combination of two signals. One comes from token-level distribution statistics, intended to capture local uncertainty during generation. The other comes from graph topology, intended to capture how that local uncertainty unfolds into global branching structure. The claim is that this joint quantity is a better estimator of reasoning uncertainty than sequence-only or self-prompting approaches.

GUT-O is the optimization component. Since full graph construction is expensive and not directly usable online during RL, the paper introduces a proxy uncertainty measure and uses its negative value as reward. The design choice is important: optimizing only answer correctness does not explicitly discourage unstable or nonsensical intermediate branches, while optimizing shallow signals such as length or entropy may not align with reasoning quality. GUT-O tries to bias the model toward trajectories that are both lower-uncertainty and still task-effective. This differs from self-consistency or reranking methods, which improve outputs at inference time by sampling more; GUT-O attempts to shift the model distribution itself.78:T4bc,From the full-text excerpts provided, GUT-Q is evaluated on 4 LLMs and 5 datasets against 45 uncertainty baselines, using selective generation as the downstream testbed and AUROC, AUPRC, and PRR as metrics. The reported result is that GUT-Q performs best overall in this comparison, suggesting that graph-based reasoning-space estimates separate reliable from unreliable generations better than single-sequence statistics or simpler diversity measures. GUT-O is tested across 4 model scales and 5 datasets, with the main finding that RL with the uncertainty proxy reduces reasoning uncertainty and also improves accuracy.

The experimental framing is stronger than a simple correlation study. The paper checks whether the uncertainty score is useful for abstention or selective answering, and then checks whether it can function as an optimization signal. That said, the main caveat is methodological cost and attribution: graph construction depends on repeated sampling plus an external NLI model. The critical question is how much of the gain comes from the graph formulation itself, versus extra sampling budget and the quality of semantic merging. The ablations around these components are therefore central.79:T4d2,For a skim-level read, start with the overview figure and the formal definition of GUT-Q, then read the reward construction in GUT-O, and finally inspect the main selective-generation table. Around 25–35 minutes should be enough to capture the main idea.

What to focus on:
1. The exact definition of reasoning uncertainty. The paper is not measuring generic predictive uncertainty; it is measuring instability in branching reasoning trajectories.
2. The graph construction pipeline. Check how step boundaries are defined, how semantic equivalence is decided with NLI, and whether logically distinct steps could be over-merged.
3. The decomposition of graph complexity. Understand what the token-statistics term contributes versus the topology term, and whether they partly measure the same phenomenon.
4. The proxy used in GUT-O. Ask whether it tracks the full graph complexity well enough to be a meaningful RL reward.
5. The ablations. The most informative ones are likely: removing NLI merging, using only topology, using only token statistics, and varying the number of samples.

If the goal is only to decide whether to follow up later, the method overview, complexity definition, and the main comparison table are sufficient.7a:T45e,The method has two main parts. First, the paper localizes refusal. Instead of treating the residual stream as the universal readout site, it distinguishes the fresh write from the accumulated residual. In transformers this is the attention output; in SSMs it is the selective-scan block output; in hybrids the relevant write sites are examined separately. Linear harm probes are trained to separate harmful from benign prompts, and the strongest decodability appears at the architecture-specific write site rather than in the accumulated residual.

Second, the paper tests cross-architecture alignment and causal transfer. It uses a Procrustes rigid rotation to align one model’s representation space to another’s, allowing only rotation, not reshaping. A refusal direction learned in a transformer is mapped into the target architecture’s space, then removed or gated at the target write site. If this transported direction still controls refusal, the result is stronger than simple linear separability: it suggests the models share a genuinely similar representation rather than merely a shared label boundary.7b:T52d,The main target model is Falcon-Mamba-7B, with Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B as transformer references, plus validation on RWKV-6 and Zamba2-7B. Several results stand out. 1) On a surface-controlled subset, a harm probe at the write site reaches AUROC 0.99, while a surface-only probe scores 0.54, indicating the probe is not just detecting jailbreak wrapper text. 2) A single rigid rotation transfers the transformer refusal direction into SSM and hybrid spaces; removing that direction weakens refusal, most clearly for the transformer-SSM pair and at the Mamba write site in Zamba2. 3) A matched-magnitude control shows that directions estimated at the write site causally control refusal, whereas directions estimated in the accumulated residual degrade substantially. 4) The detector-triggered gate is used as a causal test rather than as a defense claim. On Falcon-Mamba, prefix-injection attack success drops from 98.0% to 5.0%. Under a suffix attack optimized through the gate, the detector still fires on all 100 attacked prompts and attack success remains at 1.0%, down from 15.0%. The paper is careful to note that this gate is not stronger than a simpler baseline that always emits a fixed refusal once the detector fires. What transfers across architectures is the refusal direction, not a superior defense recipe.7c:T731,The framework has three main parts. The first is environment reconstruction. Starting from public terminal-agent trajectories, the system replays file operations and restores each file to its pre-edit state, so the resulting workspace starts unsolved. Because trajectories usually reveal only a partial view of the original workspace, replay alone produces incomplete environments. A completion agent then fills in missing files and dependencies while trying not to leak the solution. This design choice is important: it avoids generating environments from scratch, which often hurts realism, and it also avoids requiring access to the original repository, which may be unavailable.

The second part is task expansion. The framework does not only recover the original user intent; it also synthesizes new tasks over the reconstructed environment. Breadth expansion links related environments and creates cross-workspace tasks, such as porting a feature from one project to another or connecting two components. Depth expansion turns a single-round task into a multi-round interaction. After one round is completed, a user agent issues grounded follow-up requests based on the changed workspace, or asks for fixes when a round fails. This yields stateful, evolving tasks rather than static instructions.

The third part is verification and data generation. For each new task, an agent writes a verifier inside the container, and only trajectories whose tests pass are kept. Qwen3.7-Max is then used as a teacher to solve tasks again in these reconstructed environments, and the resulting trajectories are used to train Qwen3.5-27B. The key point is the data-generation paradigm: reconstruct the environment first, then let a stronger model produce fresh, verifiable solutions, instead of treating historical trajectories as final supervision.7d:T476,The reported scale is substantial. From public terminal-agent trajectories, the pipeline produces 37.3k task-sufficient environments, meaning the reconstructed workspaces are complete enough to support execution and verification rather than being partial artifacts.

Using newly generated queries over these environments and teacher rollouts from Qwen3.7-Max, the authors train Qwen3.5-27B and report gains of 11.9 points on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 13.8 points on the multi-round benchmark EvoCode-Bench v2 MT@4. This suggests the data is useful not only for single-round repair tasks but also for interactive multi-turn coding agents.

The most important experimental takeaway is the ablation: re-solving tasks in reconstructed environments clearly outperforms imitating the original raw trajectories. That result supports the paper’s central thesis that trajectories are most valuable as partial observations of environments, not as immutable demonstrations. Another important detail is that every synthesized task is paired with a verifier and filtered by test success, so the quality of executable supervision is doing a lot of the work.7e:T782,方法由两部分组成。第一部分是 dynamic per-trajectory rubric。不是为整个任务分布预先写一套固定 rubric，而是先根据任务指令生成初始 criteria，再结合每个 rollout 暴露出来的子目标、失败模式和执行路径，对 rubric 做扩展，最后把同一 group 内多个 rollout 提出的 criteria 合并成共享 rubric 集合。这样做的原因很直接：固定 rubric 往往覆盖不到长轨迹里真实发生的分叉和失败细节，而按轨迹动态生成可以让 judge 评价的是“这条轨迹实际试图完成了什么、卡在了哪里”，不是抽象模板。

第二部分是 distribution of rubric-conditioned advantage。标准 GRPO 对同一 trajectory 的所有 token 使用同一个 advantage；DRACO 改成先让 judge 对 rubric 中每个 criterion 给 verdict，再把 criterion 与轨迹中负责该 criterion 的步骤对齐，然后用一个闭式规则把 criterion-level judgment 分摊成 per-step advantage。论文强调这个分配规则满足若干形式性质，包括总量守恒、符号保持、长度无关等，目的是避免 credit 在长轨迹里被无控制地稀释，或者因为轨迹更长而系统性偏置。这里的关键不是“做 step reward”本身，而是 step reward 不依赖终局 verifier，也不依赖 learned reward model，而是直接从 rubric verdict 推出。

训练上仍然套在 GRPO 框架里：对每个任务采样一组轨迹，judge 对每条轨迹按动态 rubric 打分，再把 rubric verdict 重新分配到步骤，形成替代统一 trajectory advantage 的 step-level advantage。论文还比较了 frontier judge 与 self-judge，说明 judge 质量会直接影响 credit 质量。与已有 process reward 或 step-level RL 方法的差别在于，很多先前方法仍然锚定 gold answer、unit test 或 terminal reward；DRACO 刻意去掉了这些训练时真值依赖。7f:T6ef,DRACO has two main components. The first is dynamic per-trajectory rubric generation. Instead of writing one fixed rubric for the whole task distribution, the judge first proposes criteria from the task instruction, then extends those criteria using what each sampled rollout actually attempted, where it failed, and which subgoals emerged during execution. The criteria proposed from all trajectories in the same GRPO group are merged into a shared rubric set. The motivation is straightforward: fixed rubrics under-specify long trajectories, while rollout-conditioned rubrics can evaluate what the policy concretely did rather than what a generic template expected.

The second component is rubric-conditioned advantage redistribution. Standard GRPO assigns one scalar advantage to every token in a trajectory. DRACO asks the judge to score each rubric criterion, aligns criteria to the steps responsible for them, and then applies a closed-form redistribution rule to produce per-step advantages. The paper emphasizes several formal properties of this rule, including conservation of total push, sign preservation, and length independence. These properties are meant to prevent the usual failure mode where long trajectories dilute credit or where trajectory length itself introduces systematic bias.

Training remains within the GRPO framework: sample a group of trajectories, score them with a frozen judge under the dynamic rubric, and replace uniform trajectory-level advantage with redistributed step-level advantage. A notable design choice is that the method does not rely on a learned reward model and does not anchor step rewards to terminal verifiers or gold answers. That is the main distinction from much of the prior process-reward and step-credit literature.80:T662,The main experiments are on AppWorld. The paper states that this is the first RL training result on AppWorld that never accesses the environment’s ground-truth unit-test signal during training. On AppWorld TN, DRACO reaches 85.3 TGC@1, which is a +15.9 point gain over the untrained policy. It also transfers zero-shot to τ-bench and performs at or above a verifier-trained run under the same budget. The key point is not only the absolute score, but that outcome-blind training remains competitive with verifier-based RL.

The ablations separate the two components: dynamic rubric alone, redistribution alone with a fixed rubric, and the full method. The two parts appear complementary. Dynamic rubrics improve coverage and task adaptation, while redistribution improves signal density and credit precision. The paper also compares against a coarse outcome-reward baseline, showing that a single trajectory-level scalar is much weaker for long-horizon learning.

Another useful experiment replaces the frontier judge with a self-judge. Performance drops, but the method still works, suggesting DRACO is not entirely dependent on an extremely strong external judge. That said, judge quality clearly matters because both rubric generation and criterion verdicts feed directly into the RL signal. The paper also analyzes policy efficiency after training and the reward actually optimized by the policy, which is relevant for checking rubric overfitting or reward hacking. Not all ablation numbers are visible in the provided excerpt, but the experimental structure is centered on signal source, credit granularity, and judge quality.81:T8b7,The central idea is environment evolution. The paper starts from a multi-turn learning objective, models agent-environment interaction as a Markov process, and then introduces a higher-level decomposition of execution into alternating scenarios and skills. From this view, environment difficulty is decomposed into three factors: scenario novelty, skill rarity, and execution length. Intuitively, an environment becomes harder when it requires the agent to enter less common scenarios, apply rarer skills or skill combinations, and sustain a longer meaningful execution chain.

A key step is to move from model-dependent negative log-likelihood to a policy-independent notion of difficulty under a reference distribution T. This is meant to separate environment difficulty from model weakness. In other words, the authors do not want to define an environment as difficult merely because the current policy fails on it. With this formulation, environment generation no longer needs to depend on on-policy rollouts.

The implementation uses a loop-engineered multi-agent harness that incrementally modifies a seed environment along one of three directions: increasing scenario novelty, increasing skill rarity, or increasing execution length. Each modification must preserve executability, task validity, and the verifier. This produces verified lineages of environments with gradually increasing difficulty. The lineage design matters: instead of generating entirely new environments from scratch, the method performs local, controlled, traceable edits on already verified environments, which makes curriculum construction more manageable. Training then schedules these evolved environments generation by generation so that the policy continues to receive non-saturated learning signals over time.

Compared with co-evolution, the main differences are that the process is off-policy and that difficulty increase is explicit and structured rather than driven by current rollout failures. The trade-off is that the quality of the difficulty definition and the evolution harness becomes central: if those are weak, the system may generate environments that are harder in superficial ways but not actually more learnable or more useful.82:T612,The paper reports 200-step long-horizon RL experiments on Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, environment evolution improves performance by 14.4 and 18.0 percentage points, respectively. The authors also use Hy4 preview, Claude Opus 5, and GPT-5.6 Sol for rollout-based difficulty estimation, showing that the evolved environments remain challenging across different models rather than being overfit to a single generator or policy.

Another important result is that evolved environments continue to provide useful RL signal even after the seed environments have already been used for SFT. That suggests the method is not merely replaying the original distribution, but is actually pushing the environment family into new difficulty regimes. Compared with agent-environment co-evolution and ensemble baselines, the paper claims that off-policy evolution yields longer-lasting learning signals and slower saturation during training.

From an evaluation standpoint, the paper is trying to validate three things: whether the evolved environments are genuinely harder, whether that hardness generalizes across models, and whether the harder environments translate into downstream benchmark gains. For credibility, the most important details are likely in the validation of lineages, preservation of verifiers, and the separate effects of the three evolution directions. The headline numbers are the final benchmark gains, but the more informative evidence is probably in the difficulty calibration and training-curve persistence analyses.83:T43e,For a skim read, start with the introduction and preliminaries to understand why the paper rejects on-policy pass rate as the primary definition of difficulty. Then read the derivation of environment difficulty, focusing on why novelty, rarity, and length are the chosen factors and how the reference distribution T turns them from model-specific weaknesses into environment properties.

In the method section, pay most attention to how the multi-agent harness edits and validates environments, especially the construction of verified lineages. In the experiments, prioritize three kinds of results: cross-model difficulty estimates, evidence that the learning signal lasts longer during training, and the final gains on Terminal-Bench 2.1. If the goal is only to decide whether the idea is worth following, 25 to 35 minutes should be enough. If the goal is to assess adoption in an internal agent-training data pipeline, the appendix on environment validation, failure cases, and ablations over the three evolution directions is likely more important than the headline benchmark table.84:T517,The main technical idea is an agentic attacker equipped with a search harness. Instead of explicitly enumerating all possible payloads and injection sites, the paper treats the attack surface as a latent space induced jointly by the environment, the benign user task, and the malicious injection task. To search this space, the attacker is given reconnaissance tools of two kinds: tools for understanding the environment and task context, and tools for understanding candidate injection vectors and their constraints.

The attacker then performs structured reasoning over possible strategies, explores promising subspaces, and uses victim-agent feedback plus environment-state changes to adapt future attempts. A key design choice is explicit strategy management. The paper argues that without tracking explored directions, pruning unproductive branches, and maintaining search state, larger compute budgets lead to redundant exploration and weaker scaling. In that sense, the search harness is what turns prompt injection from one-shot payload generation into an iterative attack process. The study is conducted in a white-box environment setting, which makes the attack surface visible to the attacker and isolates the role of test-time search more cleanly; black-box transfer is left for future work.85:T451,From the available full text, the experiments are organized to show two main findings rather than to optimize a single benchmark number. First, increasing attacker test-time compute improves both vulnerability discovery and exploitation across heterogeneous tasks. This is the central empirical claim and supports the paper’s argument that fixed-budget evaluations can underestimate real-world risk. Second, ablations indicate that explicit strategy management matters: when search tracking and redundancy control are removed, gains from larger budgets degrade because the attacker wastes compute revisiting similar attack directions.

The visible content does not include enough complete tables or setup details to safely restate exact percentages, sample counts, or significance values. What is clear is that both user-task completion and attack success are evaluated through binary outcomes tied to final environment-state changes, which is a stronger setup than relying only on a language-model judge. failure mode of expert pruning in MoE models trained under excessively strong load balancing. In this regime, which the authors call over-dispersed routing, the router spreads tokens almost uniformly across experts. That breaks a key assumption behind many pruning methods: router probabilities no longer provide a meaningful importance signal. As a result, global expert scores collapse, subtle domain specialization is averaged away, and perplexity stops being a reliable proxy for downstream capability after pruning. Existing KV cache compression methods rely on recent queries to estimate future token importance, implicitly assuming these serve as reliable proxies for future attention patterns. We demonstrate that this assumptio","starred":false,"priority":"p2","reading_tier":"skim","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"2026-09-04T10:23:16Z","category_id":"efficient","cover_url":"/covers/2609_04971.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.LG","cs.CL"],"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇工作处理的是长链式推理场景下 KV cache 压缩失效的问题。已有方法通常在 eviction 时用“最近几个 query 的注意力”来估计哪些历史 token 未来还重要，默认近期注意力模式可以代表后续解码需求。论文用全文中的分析说明，这个假设在 LRM 的长程推理里并不稳：模型会在某些时刻产生一类会回看很早期上下文的 token，作者称为 Thought Revisiting Tokens，简称 TRT。它们会重新关注前面形成的计划、约束、子目标或中间结论。如果这些早期 token 已被基于局部注意力的策略提前驱逐，后续推理质量会明显下降。核心问题不是一般长上下文压缩，而是“如何在不知道未来 query 的情况下，保住那些会被未来全局回看的 KV”。","importance":"对基座研究本身，它不是预训练方法论文，但对长推理模型的部署和推理时扩展有直接价值。更具体地说，它给出一个很有用的观察：长 CoT 不是简单的局部自回归展开，而是夹杂少量但关键的“全局回访”步骤。这个现象对两类研究都有启发。第一类是 inference system：KV 压缩不能只看 recency 或最近注意力，还要建模未来可能出现的全局 query。第二类是 pretrain/post-train 接口：如果长推理能力依赖这种周期性回访，那么训练阶段是否显式鼓励计划形成、计划回访、结构化中间状态，可能会影响推理时的注意力几何。贡献量级上，这篇更像是一个扎实的推理优化方法，加上一条关于 reasoning dynamics 的经验发现。","technical_approach":"方法的关键是把 query 分成两类：一类是 local query，主要关注邻近 token；另一类是 global query，对应 TRT，会跨很长距离去看早期上下文。作者进一步发现，global query 在 query embedding 空间里不是无结构散布，而是聚成少量相似簇。基于这个几何现象，论文提出 beacon queries：用少量代表性 query 去近似未来可能出现的全局回访模式。\n\n具体做法是，在 KV eviction 时，不再只用 recent queries 给历史 token 打分，而是同时维护一组 beacon queries。每个历史 KV 的保留价值由两部分共同决定：它对近期 query 是否重要，以及它对这些 beacon queries 是否重要。这样即便当前窗口内还没出现回访行为，只要某个历史 token 对代表性全局 query 很关键，它就不容易被驱逐。\n\n难点在于 beacon query 不能靠离线聚类，因为推理是在线进行的，query 序列不断增长。为此作者设计了 Continual Farthest Point Sampling。直观上，它在推理过程中持续从已见 query 中挑选几何上彼此尽量分散的代表点，以有限内存维护一组覆盖面较广的 query 原型。相比存完整 query 历史，这个做法内存可控；相比只看最近 query，它又能保留未来全局回访所需的结构信息。\n\n从方法定位看，BeaconKV 是 training-free 的，不改模型参数，不需要额外蒸馏或校准，属于推理时 cache management。它和 RPC、R-KV 的区别不在于更复杂的 token redundancy 建模，而在于显式承认“未来 query 分布与最近 query 分布不一致”，并用少量代表性全局 query 去补这个缺口。","experiments":"实验覆盖四个开源 reasoning model：R1-Distill-Qwen-7B、R1-Distill-Llama-8B、Qwen3-4B、Qwen3-14B；任务包括 AIME24、MATH-500、LiveCodeBench、GPQA-Diamond，基本覆盖数学、代码、科学问答几类长推理负载。\n\n论文给出的主结果有几组比较关键。第一，在多种 cache budget 下，BeaconKV 一般都优于 RPC 和 R-KV，准确率提升最高可到 31.7 个百分点。这个数字说明在激进压缩区间，错误驱逐确实是主导问题，而不是简单的容量不足。第二，在强压缩设置下，峰值 GPU memory 最多可降 5.8 倍，同时准确率接近 full KV inference。第三，吞吐相对不压缩基线可提升 4.3 倍以上，说明收益不只是“能跑更长”，也包括更高 batch 或更高并发下的实际速度改善。\n\n从论文叙述看，最有信息量的消融不是单纯比方法，而是验证几个机制假设：1）TRT 确实存在，并且对应明显的远程注意力模式；2）这些 global queries 在 embedding 空间中呈簇状，而不是均匀分布；3）只靠 recent queries 无法覆盖这些未来回访需求；4）加入 beacon queries 后，被保留下来的 token 更接近 full KV 下真正高价值的 token。若读全文，建议重点看 attention 可视化、query 几何分析、以及 beacon 数量和压缩预算之间的 trade-off。","reading_guide":"这篇适合泛读，但不要只看实验表。建议先看 Introduction 里对 TRT 的定义和 failure case，再看分析部分关于 local/global query final-answe","starred":true,"priority":"p1","reading_tier":"must_read","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"2026-09-04T02:29:10Z","category_id":"eval","cover_url":"/covers/2609_04648.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.CL"],"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇工作要解决的是 rollout，保留最终答案正确的轨迹；从这些正确轨迹中抽取中间结论；再把语义等价的中间结论聚类，得到一组可验证的节点。这样得到的节点不是某一条标准解的逐步复刻，而是多条正确路径共享的“公共检查点”。这一步很关键，因为它决定了奖励信号更接近 objective completion，而不是风格模仿。基于这些节点，作者提出 ConsensusPR，把原本只在终点给出的二元奖励，沿着推理路径 能区分“是不是绕了很多无效步骤”。训练上，ConsensusPR 被设计成能直接接入现有 GRPO 和 DAPO/RLVR 管线，不需要额外训练一个 PRM。和传统 PRM 的区别在于：PRM 试图判断每一步写得好不好，ConsensusPR Headroom ranks stored groups by remaining learning value: whether the current policy still has room to move probability mass toward high-advantage responses and away from low-advantage ones. Policy Drift gates groups by compatibility with the current policy, using the generation-time policy as the reference. The minimum replay unit is a full GRPO group, not an individual response, because GRPO’s advantage signal is defined by within-group comparison. The buffer stores immutable group-level reference state: actions, generation-time log probabilities, and response-level advantages. This creates a spurious advantage signal in bounded-answer and outcome-only search settings.","importance":"The result is relevant to RLVR and reasoning post-training. GRPO is often used with binary verifiers, but its advantage magnitude depends on the correct/wrong composition inside a rollout group rather than on the causal quality of the trajectory. In multiple-choice tasks, short-answer math, enumerable subcases, and search agents with many possible paths, some correct rollouts are lucky or low-quality. If these rollouts receive high imitation weight, the policy can learn answer priors or search detours instead of robust reasoning. For foundation-model training, the broader lesson is that the structure of the post-training signal can distort conclusions about model capability.","technical_approach":"The analysis starts from binary-reward GRPO. For a group of G rollouts with rewards r_i∈{+1,-1}, let n+ and n- be the counts of correct and wrong rollouts. GRPO standardizes rewards using the within-group mean and variance. Substituting binary rewards shows that the advantage magnitude is determined by the group composition. In particular, when positives are rare, a positive rollout receives a large positive weight. The estimator cannot tell whether that positive rollout came from reasoning or from chance. The proposed estimator, SignBalance, keeps the verifier sign but replaces the composition-dependent magnitude with a global scale. It then uses stop-gradient per-class rescaling to restore batch-level zero-mean force balance. The PPO-style surrogate is left unchanged, and the method adds no parameters, external model, or inference-time cost.","experiments":"The paper highlights three regimes where the spurious component becomes large. The first is explicitly bounded-answer tasks, such as k-way multiple choice, where random guessing succeeds with probability 1/k. The second is nominally open-answer data with bounded subcases; the paper reports that 55.95% of MATH-7.5K problems admit short numeric or categorical answers. The third is search-agent training with outcome-only reward, where a larger action budget opens many redundant or invalid paths that can still end at the correct answer. Experiments span math reasoning and search-agent tasks across different model scales, and the reported pattern favors SignBalance over the standard GRPO estimator. The provided text does not include the full result tables, so the most useful reading is to check whether the gains align with reduced guessing or detour-like behavior rather than only final accuracy.","reading_guide":"Skim Sections 3.2–3.4 for the derivation and the SignBalance estimator, then inspect Table 1 for the bounded-answer analysis of MATH-7.5K and the experiment tables for task-wise differences from GRPO.
